revision: V4.2 (audited): cryptographic evidence hash binding. `evidence_hash` stopped being a replay label and became a commitment: _fetch_evidence checks it inside the non-deterministic round against the SHA-256 of the document the contract actually fetched, and a document that does not hash to it is NO_EVIDENCE -- exactly like a document that could not be read. The digest is taken over the RAW 2xx response body, not over the rendered / sanitized / truncated text the tribunal reads, so the commitment is reproducible off-chain by any client with one plain HTTP GET and a stock SHA-256, with no need to mirror _sanitize_evidence, the 1500-char truncation budget, or the runner's choice of render over GET. That closes the last gap in the read path: previously a filing named a URI and the tribunal ruled on whatever that URI served at read time, so the on-chain record could not be tied to the bytes it judged. _canon_hash also strips a leading `0x` now, because hexdigest() never carries one and every wallet and block explorer prints one -- without the strip a correctly-committed filing spelled the way a block explorer spells it would be rejected for its notation rather than its document. Builds on the V4.1.1 audited base.

deployed_code_sha256.note: GenVM is not an EVM chain, so eth_getCode returns 0x even for a live contract and cannot be used to compare deployed bytecode against source. The explorer API publishes the deploy transaction's own contract_code, which settles the question directly: sha256(base64.b64decode(deploy_tx.data.contract_code)) below is the hash of the code RUNNING at contract_address.

predecessors.revision: V4.1.1 (audited): the V4.1 hardening pass plus the 404 render gate. V4.1.1 -- _fetch_evidence runs _get_evidence_text (a plain gl.nondet.web.get) FIRST as a 2xx status gate and returns NO_EVIDENCE on anything else, then calls _render_evidence_text for the prose and falls back to the verified GET body; gl.nondet.web.render exposes no HTTP status, so with render first a 404 or 500 error page read as a document and set evidence_present, which drives _clamp_tier's third corridor -- a dead link could turn a dismissal into a 25% slash. V4.1 -- full prompt-tag isolation (every litigant-controlled prompt field wrapped in its own sanitized tag: <untrusted_evidence_data>, <covenant_terms>, <plaintiff_allegation>, <evidence_source>) and strict telemetry clamping in _clamp_tier: the MALICIOUS_REPORT floor moved from BPS_CRITICAL (7500) down to BPS_ELEVATED (2500) so a report the metric corroborates is never confiscated as a lie, and the negligible band (< 500 bps) floors CRITICAL_BREACH and ELEVATED_RISK to NORMAL with no evidence escape, so a document can never manufacture a breach out of a metric that shows none. Builds on the V4 audited base.
